kapirājacariyā.meaning_2: conduct of the monkey king; the monkey king's way of behaving
kapirājacariyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Cariyāpiṭaka; nominative singular. Sometimes treated as a dvanda-style title rather than a straightforward compound.
kapirājacariyā.translation_1: 7. The Conduct of the Monkey King

saṅkhacariyā.meaning_2: the practice of the Brahmin Saṅkha; Saṅkha's conduct
saṅkhacariyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the second chapter of the Cariyāpiṭaka. Saṅkha is the name of the Brahmin who is a former life of the Buddha. Nominative singular.

jātettha.meaning_2: born here; born in this place
jātettha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] jāta (pp of jāyati) + ettha (here). The text reads jātettha vessavīthiyā: 'I was born here in the merchants' street.'
jātettha.translation_1: I was born there in the peasant’s street,
jātettha.translation_2: I was born there in the merchant’s street, and that’s why I was called Vessantara.

kapimāgantvā.meaning_2: a monkey, having come; having arrived, the monkey
kapimāgantvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kapiṃ (accusative singular of kapi) and āgantvā (absolutive of āgacchati). Alternative analysis: kapi + māgantvā, but the sense in the Cariyāpiṭaka verse is 'a monkey having come'.
kapimāgantvā.translation_2: Then a monkey came along, wicked, ignoble, and nimble.

jinasevitaṃ.meaning_2: practised by the Victor; fostered by the Buddha; resorted to by the conqueror
jinasevitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of jina (the Buddha) + sevita (practised, resorted to). In the text it agrees with pubbakaṃ dhammaṃ (masc accusative singular) and describes the ancient Dhamma as practised by former Buddhas.
jinasevitaṃ.translation_2: Recollecting the Dhamma of the good, the ancient way fostered by former Victors,

mātaṅgacariyaṃ.meaning_2: elephant conduct; the practice of the elephant; the elephant's way of life
mātaṅgacariyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh cariyā in the Cariyāpiṭaka, referring to the Buddha's former life as an elephant. Accusative singular in the text. Sometimes resolved as mātaṅga + cariyā (fem), 'the elephant's conduct'.

sapabbataṃ.meaning_2: with mountains; together with the mountains
sapabbataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] sa- is the prefix form of saha ("with"). Accusative singular agreeing with pathaviṃ in the text.
sapabbataṃ.translation_2: The earth from sea to sea, with its forests and mountains—

paññāsasamādhikāni.meaning_2: more than fifty; fifty or more
paññāsasamādhikāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it qualifies vassāni (neuter plural), so it appears as paññāsasamādhikāni. Sandhi paññāsā + samādhika > paññāsasamādhika.
paññāsasamādhikāni.example_2: Athāparaṃ yaṃ caritaṃ mamedaṃ, vassāni paññāsasamādhikāni.
paññāsasamādhikāni.translation_2: but then, as for this behavior (caritaṃ) of mine for more than fifty years,

pūrayituṃ.meaning_2: to fill; to fulfil; to complete
pūrayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in -tuṃ of the causative pūreti. In the text it depends on demi, 'I give ... to fulfil'.
pūrayituṃ.translation_2: to fill what is lacking in my mind, I give a gift to beggars;

dandhayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative in -aya; 3rd singular in the text, preceded by mā (prohibitive). The meaning 'delays; hesitates' fits the context.
dandhayi.example_2: 63. ‘‘‘ Ehi sivaka uṭṭhehi, mā dandhayi mā pavedhayi;
dandhayi.translation_2: Come, Sivaka, get up! Do not delay, do not tremble!

pavedhayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular imperative in -yi (mā pavedhayi) used as a prohibition in the Cariyāpiṭaka verses; from the causative of √vedh, so literally 'do not make tremble, do not waver'.
pavedhayi.example_2: 63. ‘‘‘ Ehi sivaka uṭṭhehi, mā dandhayi mā pavedhayi;
pavedhayi.translation_2: Come, Sivaka, get up! Do not delay, do not tremble!

phussatiyā.meaning_2: name of the Buddha's mother in a former life; Phussatī
phussatiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of the mother; genitive singular in the text (phussatiyā kucchiṃ = into Phussatī's womb). Could also be read as a feminine noun in -ī with an irregular genitive.
phussatiyā.translation_1: Once I was conceived in the womb
phussatiyā.translation_2: Once I was conceived in the womb of my dear mother Phussatī,

nappatiguyhāmi.meaning_2: I do not hide; I do not conceal
nappatiguyhāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + paṭiguyhāmi, present 3rd singular of paṭigūhati (variant paṭiguyhati). The printed text has nappatiguyhāmi; the Burmese edition reads nappatigūhāmi. Meaning: 'I do not conceal (it)'.
nappatiguyhāmi.example_1: Santaṃ nappatigūhāmi [nappatiguyhāmi (sī. ka.)], dāne me ramate mano.
nappatiguyhāmi.translation_1: I do not hide what exists, for my mind delights in giving.’

sāvayitvā.meaning_2: having made sound; having caused to be heard; having sounded
sāvayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of sāveti (causative of suṇāti). The -y- is a glide after the causative stem sāve; the PEU split su + ṇe + tvā agrees. Object kaṇṇabheriṃ.
sāvayitvā.translation_2: sounding the drums, I gave a great offering.

paṭippathe.meaning_2: the opposite way; the way back; oncoming road
paṭippathe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, in the phrase anumagge paṭippathe "along the road and the opposite way". Occasionally written paṭipathe; the doubled -pp- is due to sandhi.
paṭippathe.translation_1: coming the other way along the road,
paṭippathe.example_2: 98. ‘‘ Ye keci manujā enti, anumagge paṭippathe;
paṭippathe.translation_2: Whatever people would come along, coming the other way along the road,

uparodanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only the 3rd plural uparodanti appears in the text. The form is unusual; the meaning 'cries' given in the sentences is accepted.
uparodanti.translation_2: for the sake of those fruits, the children cried.

sayamevoṇamitvāna.meaning_2: having bowed down of their own accord; having bent down by themselves
sayamevoṇamitvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sayam eva and the absolutive oṇamitvāna (of oṇamati, 'bends down'). In the text it describes the trees bending down before the Bodhisatta. Sometimes written sayamevoṇamitvā.
sayamevoṇamitvāna.translation_1: bent down of their own accord,
sayamevoṇamitvāna.translation_2: bending down of their own accord, approached the children.

dhītaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of dhītar (daughter), here in the phrase jāliṃ kaṇhājinaṃ dhītaṃ, listing the Buddha's children. The nominative singular is dhītā.
dhītaṃ.translation_2: Jāli, my daughter Kaṇhājinā, and Queen Maddī my devoted wife:

gavesayyuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reading gavesayyuṃ is a variant of gavesisuṃ; both are aorist 3rd plural. Commentary (ka.) gives gavesayyuṃ, evidently an aorist in -yyuṃ. Root √gaves (seek, search) is not in the given root list, so the root fields are uncertain.
gavesayyuṃ.translation_1: having prepared gifts, they sought out one worthy of offerings.

phoṭetvā.meaning_2: having shaken; having shaken off; having dusted off
phoṭetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of phoṭeti (√phuṭ 2, 'swell, burst' with causal sense 'shake, strike'); the object rajagate gatte is accusative plural. Alternative analysis √phuṭ 1.
phoṭetvā.translation_2: Shaking my dusty limbs, I sat down at one side.

ālambaṇo.meaning_2: support; object of sense; name of a man (Ālampāyana)
ālambaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written ālambaṇo, probably a variant reading of ālampāyano; nominative singular used as a proper name.
ālambaṇo.translation_1: While lying there the ingrate Ālampāyana grabbed me.

sīlānurakkhisanti.meaning_2: I guarded virtue; I protected morality
sīlānurakkhisanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sīlaṃ ('virtue') and anurakkhisaṃ, the 1st person singular aorist of anurakkhati ('guards, protects'), plus the quotative ti. The sandhi form appears in verse; the sense in the sentence is 'therefore I guarded virtue.'
sīlānurakkhisanti.translation_1: that’s why I guarded my ethics.”

kāhāmiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular future in the text (kāhāmiṃ), with an extra -ṃ; standard form kāhāmi. Verse context.
kāhāmiṃ.translation_1: How could I, even for the sake of life, do harm to another?’

nārakkhiṃ.meaning_2: did not guard; did not protect
nārakkhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi form of na + arakkhiṃ, aorist 1st singular of na rakkhati. Occurs in the refrain contrasting guarding sīla with not guarding life.
nārakkhiṃ.example_2: 59. ‘‘ Anurakkhiṃ mama sīlaṃ, nārakkhiṃ mama jīvitaṃ;
nārakkhiṃ.translation_2: I guarded my ethical conduct, I did not guard my life.

sopettha.meaning_2: that certain one also here wanders; he too moves here on the earth
sopettha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of so + api + ettha (or so pi ettha). Appears in the refrain of Cariyāpiṭaka verses. Note the word may instead be so + api + attha (there exists), but the sense 'he too here' fits the verse contexts better.
sopettha.translation_2: was also wandering on the great earth with friends and associates.

kampilāyaṃ.grammar: fem, from kappila; locative singular in the text
kampilāyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of kapilāyaṃ; locative singular of the city name Kampilā in the Pañcāla kingdom.
kampilāyaṃ.translation_1: “In the fine city of the kingdom of Pañcāla, in the capital city of Kapilā,

parirakkhitvā.meaning_2: having guarded; having protected; having watched over
parirakkhitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of parirakkhati (pari + √rakkh); the form in the text is parirakkhitvā with the same -tvā suffix. Used with jīvitaṃ in the sense of guarding one's life.
parirakkhitvā.translation_2: having protected my life, I guarded my virtues.

anurakkhisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is anurakkhisaṃ, which is first person singular aorist or future of anurakkhati, glossed by the commentary as 'I guarded'. The entry follows the dictionary convention of a present-tense headword.
anurakkhisaṃ.translation_2: having protected my life, I guarded my virtues.

pabbajjamanuyācahaṃ.meaning_2: and I begged for the going forth; I requested ordination
pabbajjamanuyācahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pabbajjaṃ (accusative of pabbajjā) + anuyācaṃ (aorist 1sg of anuyācati, to beg for) + ahaṃ; the final -ṃ of the verb is dropped before ahaṃ. Alternative analysis: pabbajjaṃ + anuyāci + ahaṃ.
pabbajjamanuyācahaṃ.translation_1: and begged permission to go forth.
pabbajjamanuyācahaṃ.translation_2: after I bowed to my mother and father, I begged for the going forth.

nisedhayitvā.meaning_2: having prevented; having prohibited; having stopped; having suppressed
nisedhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of nisedheti (√sidh 1 with the causative sign). PEU suggests √sidh 'prevent, prohibit'. Used with paccantaṃ, 'having suppressed the borderland'. An alternative form is nisedhetvā.
nisedhayitvā.translation_1: After putting an end to the border conflict,
nisedhayitvā.translation_2: After putting an end to the borderland conflict, the king spoke to the charlatan:

saṃpīḷe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, used adverbially with patiposito: 'raised in confinement'. The PEU suggests saṃpīḍa, from √pīḷ 'press, crush' with the prefix saṃ; the reading could also be analysed as a verbal form.
saṃpīḷe.translation_1: as you’ve been raised in confinement.

maddiye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the text (maddiye = 'would crush'), agreeing with maccu. PEU suggests a derivation madda + eyya; alternatively optative of maddati with -iye ending. Text reads 'maccu na maddiye'.
maddiye.translation_1: where Death will not crush me.’
maddiye.example_2: Nibbutiṃ pariyesissaṃ, yattha maṃ maccu na maddiye ’.
maddiye.translation_2: I shall seek quenching where Death will not crush me.’

parimocayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person plural aorist-like form in the text (parimocayuṃ); the present 3rd singular is parimocayati. Causative of parimuccati.
parimocayuṃ.translation_2: abandoned me in the nest and saved themselves.

āvejjetvā.meaning_2: having stirred up; having shaken; having moved; having agitated
āvejjetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā, used in the verse in the sense of stirring up or summoning up the power of the Dhamma. The form shows the causative base with the prefix ā-. Spelling āvejjetvā; some editions may read āvijjetvā.
āvejjetvā.translation_1: Inspired by the power of Dhamma,
āvejjetvā.translation_2: Reflecting on the power of Dhamma, recollecting the former Victors,

abhigajjiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is an absolutive in -iya (abhi + gajjiya), often taken as abhigajjiya = abhi + gajja + tvā. It may also be analysed as a past participle used adverbially. The PEU entry gives 'thundering'.
abhigajjiya.translation_2: As soon as this excellent truth was declared, Pajjunna thundered forth;

āsīvisamakopayi.meaning_2: angered a viper; made a viper angry
āsīvisamakopayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound verb: āsīvisaṃ (viper, accusative object) + akopayi (aorist of kopayati, 'caused to be angry', 'angered'). The caesura separates the verses. Some editions read āsīvisamakopayi as one word; the -a- is the sandhi of the object's final -aṃ before a vowel.
āsīvisamakopayi.translation_2: the child (dārako) threw a ball and angered a viper.

sokasallite.meaning_2: pierced by the dart of sorrow; stricken by the arrow of grief
sokasallite.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound glossed by the commentary as sokasallavanta ('having the dart of sorrow'). Accusative plural in the text.
sokasallite.translation_2: Your words were spoken (tyāhaṃ) by me to comfort them, in their suffering and sorrow;

pamilāpetvā.meaning_2: having made (them) wither; having caused to fade; having drained
pamilāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative pamilāpeti (√milā + *āpe, 'cause to wither, drain'). In the verse the enemies are said to have been made to wither or drained before the sacrifice.
pamilāpetvā.translation_2: Having exhausted them, he brought me for the purpose of sacrifice.

niyyādayiṃ.meaning_2: handed over; gave up; renounced; delivered
niyyādayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular in the text. The form is from niyyādeti (ni + yā + √dā, caus); the sandhi change d > y is irregular. The PEU splits it as ni + yata + ṇaya, which does not fit the usual derivation.
niyyādayiṃ.example_2: Upagantvā puraṃ rammaṃ, rajjaṃ niyyādayiṃ tadā.
niyyādayiṃ.translation_2: having approached the delightful city, I then renounced kingship.

bahubbidhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular modifying dukkhaṃ in the text.
bahubbidhaṃ.translation_1: Having thus experience many kinds of suffering
bahubbidhaṃ.example_2: Evaṃ bahubbidhaṃ dukkhaṃ, sampattī ca bahubbidhā [sampatti ca bahuvidhā (sī.), sampattiṃ ca bahuvidhaṃ (ka.)];
bahubbidhaṃ.translation_2: Thus, having experienced a variety of suffering and a variety of prosperity,

mupanāmayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text m- is sandhi with the preceding word (m + upanāmayiṃ). 1st person singular aorist.
